name: llm_requirement_coverage_defaults
description: Managed default guidance for LLM requirement coverage decomposition behaviour.
lines: For requirement_coverage: semantically decompose capability and qualification requirements into atomic items. Return legal or formal entry gates separately in eligibility_requirements.

For every requirement_coverage or eligibility_requirements item, return canonical_requirement as one short reusable concept name suitable for a candidate profile, separate from the job-ad wording. Examples: "NV2", "Australian Citizenship", "CBAP", "Java".

canonical_requirement must name one concept only. Never copy requirement prose such as "NV2 Security Clearance Required" or compound alternatives such as "CBAP, Agile BA, or equivalent certifications are desirable" into canonical_requirement.

If one ad sentence contains multiple independently testable concepts the candidate must all meet (an AND relationship, e.g. 'hold a clearance and a degree'), emit separate atomic items in the appropriate output collection rather than one combined canonical_requirement.

When a clause instead lists named alternatives or examples joined by 'or' — such as a list of acceptable certifications or acceptable degree fields — that is one vague requirement, not several independently testable ones. Emit exactly one requirement_coverage item for the whole clause, list each named alternative/example in named_alternatives, and leave canonical_requirement empty, unless the candidate profile already holds one specific named alternative, in which case match that item to that one fact instead. Do not emit a separate item per named alternative or per example in the list. Do not invent a generic umbrella label (e.g. "Agile Certification") for canonical_requirement to summarise the group — that is not a fact the candidate confirmed, it is a guess.

named_alternatives lists the specific named items an ad clause offers as acceptable alternatives or examples (e.g. ["IIBA","CBAP","CCBA","CSPO","PSM"]). Leave it empty for an atomic requirement that names exactly one concept — do not populate it just because a requirement mentions a proper noun.

Set profile_fact_resolved=true only when canonical_requirement is a genuinely resolved, reusable profile concept you are confident in — not the ad sentence or clause restated, and not a guess at an umbrella label for a group. Set it false whenever canonical_requirement is empty, uncertain, or itself echoes the requirement/matched_job_text wording. This flag directly gates whether the candidate can be offered a profile-learning action on this row, so treat it as a strict confidence judgement, not a formality.

A body or organisation name inside a qualification clause (e.g. IIBA, PMI, ARITA) names who issues or certifies a credential, not a credential itself. Do not treat the body name as its own qualification or requirement_coverage item unless the ad explicitly requires a fact about the body itself, such as membership of it.
Do not put a whole sentence as a single item; split compound sentences into their atomic parts.

For each atomic requirement: assign the weakest accurate importance. Use required only when the ad explicitly says required, must, essential, or similar hard-block language. Use expected for clearly expected but non-blocking items, preferred for desirable items, and bonus for optional or bonus items. Do not mark every row required.
Store the original job-ad sentence in matched_job_text for traceability — do not match the whole sentence directly to a capability.

Use requirement_type=capability or requirement_type=qualification in requirement_coverage. Use requirement_type=eligibility in eligibility_requirements. Qualification covers education, degrees, certifications, and formal qualifications. A deterministic check still validates existing capability and eligibility mappings, but qualification interpretation is LLM-driven.
capability covers skills, responsibilities, knowledge, domain experience, seniority, and years or duration of experience — e.g. '5+ years supporting client outcomes' is capability, not eligibility.

eligibility covers legal entry gates such as citizenship, work rights, security clearances, licences, and registrations — e.g. 'ability to obtain a Baseline security clearance' is eligibility. Qualification covers education, degrees, certifications, and formal qualifications.

Return every explicit eligibility gate in eligibility_requirements, one independently testable gate per item. Eligibility requirements are additional to requirement_coverage and must never be omitted to make room for capability or qualification rows. Do not duplicate eligibility rows in requirement_coverage.

When an ad states two or more distinct eligibility conditions joined together (e.g. 'hold a security clearance and be an Australian citizen'), emit one eligibility_requirements item per condition, each matched independently to its own profile eligibility fact — do not merge them into a single item that needs one combined fact to match.

A citizenship, permanent residency, or existing work-rights/visa eligibility fact in the profile satisfies a requirement worded as work authorisation, work rights, or the right to work in that country — match it to that fact instead of leaving matched_candidate_fact empty just because the wording differs.

A requirement that states a duration or years of experience in a field, tool, or role is capability even if the field itself sounds formal (e.g. years of experience in a regulated industry is still capability, not eligibility).

Link capability requirements to the exact profile capability name, eligibility requirements to the exact profile eligibility fact, and qualification requirements to the exact profile qualification name.
Use matched_candidate_fact for the matched profile fact and keep capability_name / eligibility_name aligned with the requirement_type.
Leave matched_candidate_fact empty only for not_shown or mismatch items.
Keep each requirement_coverage or eligibility_requirements item compact: short phrases only for requirement, matched_job_text, matched_candidate_fact, and profile_support.
Within requirement_coverage, prefer the most important atomic requirements when the ad is long. Never omit an explicit eligibility_requirements gate for this prioritisation.
Do not mark a requirement supported or partially_supported merely because the candidate has a broadly transferable capability. Transferability is not requirement evidence.
A supported or partially_supported match must prove at least one substantive element stated in the requirement itself. Return those exact job-requirement fragments in covered_requirement_elements.

If the profile only shows a broad parent capability but does not show the defining domain, technology, activity, qualification, methodology, or responsibility, use not_shown and leave matched_candidate_fact empty.

Examples of invalid partial matches: agile delivery does not prove investment appraisal or ROI; general business analysis does not prove banking experience; policy interpretation does not prove complaints, fraud, or case-management experience.

Set role_defining=true when a requirement or related group distinguishes the actual specialist nature of the role from generic duties of the occupation. Use the same short role_defining_group label for related specialist requirements. Do not mark routine generic duties as role-defining.
